newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close higher amid China rumors.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close higher amid China rumors.

text.p: CBOT soy products closed higher on Wednesday, boosted by persistent rumors China was looking to buy soymeal and by forecasts for weather-related harvest delays, traders said.
Soyoil futures jumped to the day's highs late on speculative buying interest, traders said. Oil/meal spreading was also noted with most buying soymeal and selling soyoil.
Forecasts called for rain and snow across much of the eastern U.S. Midwest with drier conditions to the west. Another rain event was expected by the weekend, further slowing harvest progress.
Talk China had bought 11,000 tonnes Indian soymeal and was looking to make additional purchases also boosted soymeal futures with the strongest gains notched in the deferreds.
Soyoil ended up 0.15 to 0.25 cent a lb with December up 0.22 at 23.53 cents. Soymeal closed $2.20 to $4.30 a ton higher with December up $3.00 at $228.20 a ton.
Soymeal volume was estimated at 24,000 lots versus 27,913 Tuesday while soyoil volume was pegged at 15,000 lots versus 15,038 on Tuesday, CBOT reported.
